display_title: Official Review of Paper2400 by Reviewer ZHwx

content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper:
This paper presents a new framework for domain generalization (DG) using imbalance source (training) domains. The framework consists of two parts: style balancing and test-time style shifting. The style balancing aims at balancing populations of domain-class pairs by transforming part of data of major domain-class pairs to those of minor pairs. The test-time style shifting transforms a test example to another that looks like one of source domain data while keeping its content  The underlying assumption of these techniques is that the characteristics of a visual domain are represented by styles of its images, and that such styles are captured by channel-wise global statistics of convolutional features. 

The proposed framework is seamlessly coupled with a few DG techniques based on style augmentation, and has achieved decent performance on benchmarks with and without the cross-domain imbalance.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
[Strengths]

The proposed framework is seamlessly integrated with style-based DG methods and achieves top records in multiple benchmarks. I in particular appreciate its outstanding performance on DomainBed.


[Weaknesses]

- The problem setting looks contrived. In my view, cross-domain imbalance in training is not a big issue in real application scenarios as it can be alleviated by collecting training data carefully. In particular for image classification, the main application scenario of the paper, the cost of dataset collection is not expensive. One may argue that data of some visual domains could be rare, but the goal of DG is to learn a model well generalizing to any arbitrary unseen test domains and in this context it is not necessary to collect training data of rare domains for improving generalization capability of learned models; common and diverse domains could be more appropriate than such rare domains for DG.
- Due to the above concern, I believe, to demonstrate the value of the proposed method, it should also be evaluated on common DG benchmarks, e.g., Office-Home and DomainNet, that are not intentionally imbalanced. Hence, I recommend the authors to conduct more experiments and analysis on such benchmarks. 
- The proposed method imposes large computations additionally. The style balancing computes distances of every pair of data for each domain-class pair, which will be highly costly when the number of training data is large. Also, the test-time style shifting demands additional computation and memory footprint for finding the source domain closest to test input in terms of style; this will be also expensive when the number of source domains is large. 
- The overall pipeline of the method is complicated, tuned carefully by hand, and not fully justified. Is the way of balancing populations of domain-class pairs, based on pairwise style-differences of training data, the best? Does this greedy approach have any side-effects? Also, why does the inequality condition in Eq. (8) depend on the distance between the mean style of all source domains and and the mean style of each source domain? Is it OK to compute distances between mean styles without considering distributions/manifolds of style factors although the distributions of style factors could be anisotropic?
- The proposed method depends heavily on the coupled DG method. It can be seamlessly integrated with existing methods, but at the same time it lacks in terms of novelty and contribution in DG perspective as it modifies existing methods to focus only on a specific application scenario (which looks not very realistic as aforementioned).
- The proposed method is not compared with a recent previous work, Style Neophile (CVPR 2022), which is cited in the paper though. Style Neophile is closely related to the proposed method since it achieves DG by style injection too and may address the cross-domain data imbalance issue by synthesizing styles that have been never seen in source domains.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
- Clarity and reproducibility – Good: 

Overall the manuscript is written clearly, and elaborate on technical details for reproducing the reported results. (Minor comments: Eq. (3) looks redundant.)

- Novelty and quality – Unsatisfactory: 

I would argue that the novelty of this paper is not strong enough. Style augmentation for domain generalization is nowadays common, and the proposed method depends heavily on existing work to achieve DG. The two main components of the paper, style balancing and test-time style shifting, have originality but are not well justified, overly complicated, and focusing only on a specific application scenario that does not look very realistic/useful.
content.summary_of_the_review: The major weaknesses of the paper include contrived problem setting, lack of experiments, lack of justification for the proposed method, and incremental novelty. Although the proposed method achieved outstanding performance, it has been evaluated on intentionally imbalanced benchmarks in most cases and not compared with closely related work. For these reasons, I believe the paper does not meet the standard of ICLR and thus recommend rejection.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper considers the problem of domain generalization. To solve this problem, the authors propose style balancing to balance the samples across domains as well as test-time style shifting to stylize the test sample to the source one. Experiments on several dataset show the benefits of both style balancing and test-time style shifting.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
+ This paper is well-written and easy to follow. The motivation is clear and reasonable.

+ A good analysis of existing methods is provided, which shows the two issues of them.

+ Two strategies are proposed for domain generalization, which are easy to implement and can be applied to different methods without significant modification.

+ Extensive experiments are provided to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed method. 

+ Source code is provided.


- Although the proposed issue of imbalance is interesting, the authors seem to deliberately conduct the seriously imbalanced datasets (removing 80% data) to enable the proposed method to be beneficial. The proposed SB can commonly achieve a good improvement in imbalanced settings. However, the improvement of it commonly is limited in the traditional datasets. Hence, I doubt the practicability of the proposed method. 

- The improvement of the proposed TS is limited in most cases. Considering that it requires searching the nearest source domain during testing, I also have a concern about its practicability.

- Results of single domain generalization are missed, e.g., single-DG on PACS.

Clarity and Quality: This paper is easy to follow and well-written. Extensive experiments are provided.

Novelty: The issues raised by this paper are interesting and novel.

Reproducibility: The proposed two methods are easy to implement. Source code is provided for reproduction.

However, the authors seem to deliberately conduct the seriously imbalanced datasets (removing 80% data) to enable the proposed method to be beneficial. In addition, the improvements sometimes are limited, especially in traditional benchmarks. Considering these factors, I tend to give the borderline reject.

content.confidence: 2: You are willing to defend your assessment, but it is quite likely that you did not understand the central parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work. Math/other details were not carefully checked.
content.summary_of_the_paper: In this paper, the authors propose a couple of style balancing and test-time style shifting schemes to address the current issues of cross-domain data/class unbalancing and the source-target-domain gap. The proposed style balancing method specifically balances the number of samples for each class in the style space, whereas test-time style shifting shifts the style of the testing data to the nearest source domain that is familiar to the model. The devised two schemes are complementary to each other, which achieve gratifying results according to the experiments on two benchmarks.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
**Pros:**
- The proposed method is well-motivated.
- I appreciate the detailed analysis for the proposed method.
- Code is provided.

**Cons:**
- **Motivation:** The authors clearly demonstrate the cross-domain data/class imbalanced issue in Sect. 1 as one of the motivations for the proposed method, which is appreciated. However, the authors only show this observation with MixStyle, which is somewhat not that convincing. Will EFDMix also lead to this dilemma? Also, the authors do not mention how the previous methods consider this issue and whether there are any possible solutions with existing class-balancing method.
- **Discussion with prior work:** To my knowledge, this paper is not the first one that targets balancing in domain adaption, [a, b], just to name a few. The authors are suggested to explicitly explain the difference between these methods and how and why the proposed one achieves superior performance. For example, [a] also relies on style-based method for domain adaption.
[a] Test-time Fourier Style Calibration for Domain Generalization, IJCAI
[b] Balancing Discriminability and Transferability for Source-Free Domain Adaptation, ICML

Domain generalization is not my primary research area. Currently, it seems that the authors try to elaborate every detail of the proposed method, which make the proposed method technically sound.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
- The paper is well-written and easy to follow.
- The proposed method seems novel.
content.summary_of_the_review: I appreciate the authors' detailed discussions on each aspects of the proposed method. But since DG is not my primary area, I may refer to the comments from other reviewers for my final rating.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper targets at addressing class/data imbalance problem in domain generalization (DG), e.g., the number of samples of a source domain is relatively small and that of another domain is relatively large. It proposes a style balancing method by shifting the “large-domain” samples to the style of “small-domain” samples. The proposed technique is combined with existing style-augmentation based DG methods, formulating the pipeline of “balancing first then augmentation”, and achieves good improvements on imbalanced DG settings. Additionally, the paper proposes a test-time style shifting method to further improve performance. Extensive experiments are conducted to evaluate the proposed method.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
(1)	The paper is well written and easy to follow. 
(2)	The imbalance DG setting considered is meaningful and the proposed style balancing (SB) method that shifts the large domain style to a small domain is interesting and makes sense.
(3)	When combined with several style augmentation DG methods, the proposed SB module works well on the constructed imbalanced DG datasets.
(4)	The proposed test-time shifting (TS) is experimentally validated effective on both original and imbalanced DG settings, and works well combined with SB on the imbalance DG.
Weaknesses:
(1)	The constructed dataset is heavily imbalanced on both class/data imbalance settings, e.g., 80 percentage of two-domain samples are removed in the data imbalance case, and some class are totally missing in some source domains in the class imbalance case. Noticed that the proposed SB doesn’t make considerable improvements on the original DG settings as in Tab.2, I doubt that the robustness of the proposed SB to the imbalance ratio, authors could study the imbalance setting more than in the current paper, e.g., ratio of removed samples or missing ratio of a specific class in the data/class imbalance setting respectively.
(2)	The author claims that the TS is complementary with SB, experiments on imbalanced DG datasets do validate the combined method. However, I don’t see significant connection between these two techniques, the proposed algorithm is very heuristic, and there lacks some intuition behind these two techniques.  
(3)	The hyperparameter $\alpha$ in the TS module is not suitable with non-zero values, unless a convincible hyperparameter selection process is conducted, since one shouldn’t use target domain data for selecting the optimal hyperparameters. I think all experiments in the main paper with “+TS” or “+SB+TS” should be reconducted with zero $\alpha$, in this situation all target domain samples are shifted to a source style.
(4)	The stableness of the reported metrics is not clear, previous methods Mixstyle and EFDMix both represent the results with the format of $mean \pm var$, while it’s not clear that the reported result is mean result or best result.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The proposed technique is novel and well clarified, I can’t judge reproducibility without source codes.
content.summary_of_the_review: Authors should study more on the imbalanced DG problem, since this is not studied well before, and validate connection between SB and TS not only experimentally.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.title: Response to All Reviewers
content.comment:
We appreciate all the reviewers for providing constructive comments, which has greatly helped us to improve the paper. Below, we provide answers to the major comments raised by the reviewers.

**Impact of SB with varying portion of removed data:** This is an important/interesting comment. We performed additional experiments by varying the percentage of removed samples of the minor domains (except the largest domain). The removed percentages are 0%, 20%, 30%, 50%, 80%. The results are as follows:

|       Portion of removed data        | 0% (original)   | 20% | 30% |50% | 80%  |
|---------------|-------|---------|-------|--------|-------|
| Mixstyle      | 82.98 | 82.48   | 82.37| 80.46  | 75.65 |
| Mixstyle + SB |83.11| 82.95   | 82.79 | 81.56  | 78.45 |
| Mixstyle + TS          | 84.28| 83.73  | 83.86 |82.38  | 77.94 |
| Mixstyle + SB + TS    |**84.63** | **84.37**   | **84.24** | **83.22**  | **80.69** |

It can be seen that the gain of SB becomes larger as the portion of removed samples increases, i.e., as the dataset becomes more severely imbalanced. It can be also seen that the TS module is effective for all cases.


**Impact of TS and computational complexity:** The proposed TS is especially effective in improving the performance of the domain that has a large style gap with other domains (e.g., Sketch domain in PACS dataset). Compared to the existing test-time adaptation ideas, our scheme requires less computational burden at testing since only AdaIN is required without any model update process in our method. A more details on the complexity analysis of our SB and TS modules are provided in Appendix A.13.


**Connection between SB and TS:** We appreciate this comment. Intuitively, to maximize the advantage/effect of TS, it is important to construct a model well-trained on all source domains (for each class), which can be achieved by applying our SB during training. Without SB, the performance of TS could be sometimes limited as shown in Table 2 of our main manuscript.  


**Results on single-domain generalization:** We appreciate the reviewer’s constructive suggestion about single-source domain generalization. We performed additional experiments in a single-domain generalization setup using the PACS dataset. The model is trained on one source domain, and evaluated on the remaining three domains. Since there is only one source domain during training, we do not consider SB module in this setup. We shift the style statistics of test samples to the source domain that the model is already familiar with. As shown in the table below, since most of the test samples are considerably far away from the source domain in the single DG setup, our proposed TS module brings the significantly large performance gain without any additional training, confirming the effectiveness of our TS scheme. 

|               | Art   | Cartoon | Photo | Sketch | Avg.  |
|---------------|-------|---------|-------|--------|-------|
| Mixstyle      | 64.32 | 71.77   | 42.98 | 32.18  | 52.81 |
| Mixstyle + TS | 72.19 | 77.25   | 48.50 | 43.62  | **60.39** |
| DSU           | 64.85 | 74.53   | 39.48 | 36.20  | 53.77 |
| DSU + TS      | 70.99 | 73.95   | 51.18 | 49.03  | **61.28** |
| EFDMix        | 66.56 | 73.93   | 44.74 | 36.36  | 55.40 |
| EFDMix + TS   | 73.87 | 76.79   | 53.04 | 49.41  | **63.28** |



**Collecting training data carefully in a DG setup:** Compared to the conventional setup with a single domain, carefully collecting training data becomes much more challenging in a DG setup with multiple domains. Even in the conventional single domain setup, various long-tailed learning and class-imbalanced learning strategies have been actively studied for the past few years, motivated by the challenge of collecting rare data/classes. We claim that collecting data becomes more challenging in a multi-domain setup where rare classes are different for each source domain.
